Subject: Next steps: benchmark harness & SLO alignment for Acme AI pilot

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a reproducible baseline and SLOs for the pilot:

Summary of SLO targets discussed:
- P99 end-to-end latency (response-complete) <= 150 ms for single-turn text gen in our streaming configuration
- Time-to-first-byte (token streaming start) target <= 25 ms (when streaming enabled)
- Sustained throughput target: 100 requests/s observed with concurrency of 40 (closed-loop client)
- Availability: 99.95% during reserved window (we can dial this in for Dedicated)

Benchmarking / reproducibility asks:
- We need a shared prompt set (seed) representative of Acme queries — I attached acme_prompt_seed.csv as a starting point
- Define exact measurement definitions (TTFB vs TTC, tokenization version, RNG seeds, token limits)
- Agree on harness: do you want us to run Redwood-hosted runs or do you want a runbook so you can run locally?

Proposed timeline:
- Fri (2025-07-18): Acme shares expanded prompt set OR approves the attached seed
- Mon (2025-07-21): Agree measurement definitions and harness config
- Wed (2025-07-23): Redwood runs baseline and produces an SLO candidate table and artifacts

Action items:
- Alice / John: confirm whether token streaming requirement is start-byte (TTFB) or full token pacing requirement
- Acme: share any internal eval harness or tooling we should integrate with (links ok)
- Marissa: provision the harness and baseline config on our side (cc'd)

Attachments: acme_prompt_seed.csv, prelim_slo_table.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on a short tech sync if useful.

—Sean

Subject: Re: Next steps: benchmark harness & SLO alignment for Acme AI pilot

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side:

1) Streaming requirement: when we say "streaming enabled" we mean that the client should receive tokens progressively and the first token should arrive fast. Our internal definition is time-to-first-byte (TTFB) <= 25 ms from server start-of-response. Full token pacing is secondary for now.

2) Latency definition: is P99 computed on time-to-completion (complete response) or on time-to-first-byte? For our SLAs we typically track both; if you can capture both metrics in the baseline that would be ideal.

3) Harness: we have an internal eval harness (https://git.acme.ai/evals/stream-harness) that includes our prompt corpora and post-processing. We can share access; would you prefer to pull our harness into your runner or for us to run with Redwood-provided Docker image?

We can aim to send a broader prompt corpus by EOD Thu (2025-07-17). Also happy to do a 30-min technical sync (Marissa + Markus + engineering) to align measurement definitions — Wed morning works for us.

Copying in technical details and a lightweight runbook. Quick notes on reproducibility and what we'll provide from Redwood:

Benchmark harness & reproducibility checklist (high level):
- Measurement definitions we use by default:
  * Time-to-first-byte (TTFB): timestamp from request arrival at gateway to first token byte delivered to client
  * Time-to-completion (TTC): timestamp from request arrival to final token delivered (response-complete)
  * P50/P90/P99 computed over TTC and TTFB separately; latency buckets reported both per-request and per-token where relevant
  * Throughput: measured with a closed-loop client driver that maintains N concurrent in-flight requests; sustained throughput is the max observed stable Req/s over a 10-minute window
- Reproducibility knobs:
  * Tokenizer version pinned (we list exact commit/tag in the instructions)
  * RNG seed for sampling / temperature-controlled runs (seed provided in harness config)
  * Fixed max_tokens and stop sequences as in attached benchmark_instructions.md
  * Hardware annotations: GPU model, CUDA/cuDNN versions, and quantization profile recorded in artifacts
- Artifacts we will produce:
  * Raw measurement logs (per-request), aggregated latency histograms, and a reproducible script to re-run the baseline
  * Docker image: gcr.io/redwood-bench/redwood-runner:acme-202507 (we can share creds for a read-only pull)

Attachments: benchmark_instructions.md (contains commands, example config, tokenizer commit, and seed list)

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa (Redwood): create a short tech-run checklist and share the Docker pull + example config by EOD Tue
- Acme: share the fuller prompt corpus and any post-processing rules by Thu (2025-07-17)
- Schedule: 1-hr deep-dive Wed 2025-07-23 10:00 AM PT (Marissa / Markus / Redwood infra + Acme engs) — calendar invite to follow

If you'd like, we can also do a canary run on Redwood-hosted infra and give you the raw logs so your team can validate post-processing separately.

—Marissa
